Choosing beans for cold brew is more forgiving than for espresso, but the roast level still changes the cup dramatically. Medium and medium-dark roasts give the chocolate and caramel notes most people expect from the immersion method, while light roasts keep their fruit but can taste sour when steeped cold.
Freshness matters less than with hot brewing because the low temperature extracts fewer of the volatile aromatics anyway. Beans roasted within the last month are ideal, and anything older than three months will taste flat no matter how carefully you steep it.
Grind the beans coarse and use a scale for the ratio, because scoops of different roasts weigh very different amounts. A kitchen scale that reads to a single gram is enough precision for the whole immersion process from start to finish.
Single origin beans from Brazil and Colombia are dependable choices for a first batch, with low acidity and heavy body that survive dilution over ice without disappearing into the water.
